This integration reads the waste collection calendar that
[RecycleApp](https://www.recycleapp.be) (Fost Plus) publishes for a Belgian
address, and makes it usable in Gladys: devices, scenes and a dashboard widget.

No account, no key: the integration calls the same public API as the
recycleapp.be website. It only needs Internet access (**cloud** badge).

## Installation

1. Install **RecycleApp** from the Gladys integration catalog (Gladys 5.3.0 or later).
2. In **Configuration**, fill in:
   - **Zip code**: for example `5000`;
   - **Street**: the street name in French, Dutch or German, as RecycleApp
     writes it (case and accents do not matter);
   - **House number**.
3. Press **Test the connection**: the answer gives the address found, the waste
   types and the next collection.
4. In the **Discovery** tab, add the devices you want.

Cannot find your street? Use **Find my street**: type part of the name (for
example `fer`), the answer lists the streets RecycleApp knows in your zip code.
Copy the right name into the **Street** field.

> Some municipalities (Brussels-Capital in particular) do not publish their
> calendar on RecycleApp. If **Test the connection** finds no collection, check
> on recycleapp.be that your address has a calendar there.

## Settings

| Setting                            | Default | What it does                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Language of the waste types        | French  | Language of the device names, their states and the scene variables (fr, nl, de, en). |
| Reminder time (the evening before) | 19:00   | Belgian time of the "Waste collection tomorrow" trigger.                             |
| Time of the collection-day trigger | 07:00   | Belgian time of the "Waste collection today" trigger.                                |
| Days read ahead                    | 60      | How far ahead the calendar is read (7 to 365 days).                                  |
| Refresh interval (h)               | 12      | Hours between two reads of RecycleApp (1 to 48).                                     |

Times are written `19:00`, `19h00` or `7:00`.

## Devices

- **Next waste collection** (summary):
  - _Days until the collection_: 0 = today, 1 = tomorrow…;
  - _Collection day_: for example "Friday 23 October";
  - _Waste collected_: for example "PMD and Paper-cardboard".
- **PMD collection**, **Paper-cardboard collection**… (one per waste type):
  - _Days until the collection_;
  - _Collection day_.

A waste type with no collection in the window read (Christmas trees in summer)
shows **-1** and "No collection planned".

The values change at midnight (Belgian time). When RecycleApp stops answering,
the last calendar read is still used: the cloud badge turns degraded (orange
dot) and tells the date of the last read.

## Scenes

### Triggers

| Trigger                                  | When                                                       | Variables                    |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Waste collection tomorrow                | The evening before, at the reminder time, once for the day | `fractions`, `count`, `date` |
| A given waste type is collected tomorrow | The evening before, at the reminder time, for that type    | `fraction`, `date`           |
| Waste collection today                   | In the morning, at the time set, once for the day          | `fractions`, `count`, `date` |

Example: "Waste collection tomorrow" → send a message
`Tomorrow: {{triggerEvent.data.fractions}}, put the bins out!`

Each trigger fires once a day, even after a restart. When Gladys or the
integration restarts after the time set, the trigger still fires, up to 4 hours
later.

### Actions

- **Get the next waste collection**: for one waste type (or any when the field
  is empty), returns `found`, `days` (-1 when none), `date` (YYYY-MM-DD) and
  `fractions`, for the following actions and conditions.
- **Read the waste calendar again**: asks RecycleApp now and returns
  `collections`, `next_date` and `next_fractions`.

## Dashboard widget

The **Waste collections** widget shows the next collection, the following ones
with their RecycleApp logo and the days left, the address and the date of the
last read. The **Refresh** button reads the calendar again. Setting: how many
collections are shown (1 to 8). Waste types are named in each user's language
when RecycleApp has it.

## Troubleshooting

- **"RecycleApp does not know the zip code"**: check the zip code.
- **"No street …"** or **"Several streets match"**: use **Find my street** and
  copy the exact name.
- **No collection**: check the house number, or whether your municipality
  publishes its calendar on RecycleApp.
- **"RecycleApp could not be read"**: RecycleApp or the Internet does not
  answer. The integration retries every 15 minutes and keeps the last calendar.

The calendar read and the triggers already sent are kept in `/data`, the only
folder the container can write to.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings RecycleApp asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | The integration reads the waste collection calendar RecycleApp (Fost Plus) publishes for a Belgian address: no account, no key. Type your address as on recycleapp.be, then press "Test the connection". One device per waste type, plus the next collection, appear in the Discovery tab. |
| Zip code | `string` | Yes |  |
| Street | `string` | Yes | The street name in French, Dutch or German, as RecycleApp writes it. Not sure? "Find my street" lists the streets of your zip code. |
| House number | `string` | Yes |  |
| Language of the waste types | `select` | No | The language the waste types are named in: device names, device states and scene variables. The dashboard widget follows the language of each user. |
| Reminder time (the evening before) | `string` | No | When the "Collection tomorrow" scene trigger fires, Belgian time, HH:MM. |
| Time of the collection-day trigger | `string` | No | When the "Collection today" scene trigger fires, Belgian time, HH:MM. |
| Days read ahead | `number` | No | How far ahead the calendar is read, in days. A waste type with no collection in that window shows -1. |
| Refresh interval (h) | `number` | No | Hours between two reads of RecycleApp. A calendar changes a few times a year: 12 hours is plenty. |

## How to install RecycleApp in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: RecycleApp appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/prohand/gladys-recycleapp:1.1.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/prohand/gladys-recycleapp](https://github.com/prohand/gladys-recycleapp).

RecycleApp requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

RecycleApp is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [prohand](https://github.com/prohand), not by the Gladys core team.
